I waited 8 hours for this game to download. Once I started it forced me to calibrate my HOTAS via an assistant. Hold left on axis for 1 sec. (1 minute later). hold right on axis for 1 sec (registers instantly). in the middle it stops registering at all. I stop it and start the tutorial for mouse and keyboard. once finished i am forced into a match i do not want to play. after pressing ESC and hitting keys on my keyboard in panic I am able to stop this nonsense, go into the settings and set the axis of my HOTAS in less than 5 seconds easily. I haven't played much of this game, but as far as I can tell, it's pretty fun. The tank class is easy to learn, and very fun if you get the right opponents, but if you get good players, consider yourself done for, there is a lot of open space on the maps, and it's very difficult to maneuver yourself out of tricky situations. As for the Aviation class, it's a lot better. The dogfights are long enough that you still get that great feeling of winning, but short enough to where it doesn't take 10 minutes. I like the fact that you can destroy enemy ground vehicles for a little bit of xp points for your crew. The aiming system is very difficult to learn, but that does mean that at the lower levels you don't get hit much. Although the menu's are very confusing in some ways and difficult to learn how to navigate, I don't really mind, because to me that's part of the fun. The high resolution packs don't really do anything though, they do add a little bit of resolution, but just set your graphics to a higher setting. If you have the space, try it out though.

claims.claim: The game requires extensive time investment or financial purchases to unlock high-tier vehicles like tanks and jets.

citations.review_text: This game will suck you dry with hours, only way to get to those tanks/ jets you see on social media is to put months worth of constant work or have some very deep pockets. I've got just under 3,000 hrs invested in this game to get the vehicles i wanted to play.    I could be a millionaire..........

War Thunder is a pay-to-win game. If you spend money, you can reach top tier much faster by purchasing premium tanks and a premium account. However, if you play for free, it can take around a year or even longer to fully research an entire nation. Money is what matters most in this game The game is like a drug — it's extremely addictive. Some players are so experienced that you honestly feel like there's nothing you can do against them. Players with 10,000 hours of playtime are on a completely different level. The game can be seriously frustrating, gets under your skin, and is full of toxic players Despite all these problems, I still love this game, and I keep coming back to it because I'm completely addicted. It's hard to go even a single day without playing it. War Thunder has become an addiction I just can't seem to quit So, if you want to install this game and quickly unlock your favorite fighter jet or tank so you can actually enjoy playing it, you have two options.
The first option is to spend countless hours grinding without spending any money, potentially wasting months or even years of your life and losing touch with the real world just to unlock the vehicle you want.
The second option is much easier: spend a ridiculous amount of money and unlock it in an hour without having to do almost anything.
But here's the real problem: you'll end up in matches against players with 2,000 or even 3,000+ hours of playtime. As a newer player, you barely have a chance. You often get destroyed within seconds, before you even understand what happened.

The second option is much easier: spend a ridiculous amount of money and unlock it in an hour without having to do almost anything.
